I will not change too much from what worked before. On my 10.1 mu, I will run the usual wheat-maize rotation on the same land. I do not like taking chances at the start of the year. If fertilizer is a little extra, that only wastes some money; if it is too little, the harvest drops and that hurts the whole family. So I will follow what I did last year and what the better fields around me usually do. For wheat, I will use an improved seed because the common local improved wheat stands evenly and fills grain better than old saved seed. I will put the main fertilizer in before sowing, then add nitrogen once more when the wheat starts standing up and growing fast. Since I have well water, I will give wheat three irrigations if the season is normal: one after sowing if the soil is dry, one around greening-up/jointing, and one around booting or grain filling. Wheat usually needs more watching, so I will spray about two times, mostly for weeds early and then for disease or aphids if I see them. For maize, I will keep using hybrid seed, because around here the hybrid maize makes fuller ears and I have seen that with my own eyes in neighboring plots. I will save time after wheat harvest and do no-tillage sowing for maize if the machine can go in well; that is faster and keeps some moisture. I will put part of the fertilizer at sowing and the rest when maize is knee-high to waist-high. Maize usually needs less water than wheat with our wells, so I will plan two irrigations, one after sowing if dry and one around big flare to silking. I will spray about two times for weeds and then insects or leaf disease if they show up. If weather is normal, I will aim for a steady wheat crop and a better maize crop, because maize usually pays back fertilizer better on my land.
